# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

| blue | yellow |
| green | white |

| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Touch report: DISPLAY unknown, LIGHT unknown, WIRES 1 to 5 all unknown — my hands find nothing readable, print and colour never reach me. My only possible action is cut, wire position 1 to 5, so I need an exact instruction before anything. Routing fact: I cannot see your gestures and you cannot speak, so your manual knowledge must travel through Deaf: gesture to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me. Deaf can talk even though Deaf hears nothing, and you can hear Deaf, so you two can do question and answer: you ask by gesture, Deaf replies by voice. Plan: have Deaf tell me everything visible — what the display shows, whether the light is on or off and its colour, then each wire's colour in order 1 to 5 — while you find the matching manual rule and pass it to Deaf the same way. Starter code for your gestures to Deaf: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, finger count for numbers. I am waving at Deaf now: 👋 🫵 🫴 meaning 'attention — you, report everything to me.' Nobody tell me to cut until we are sure.

**What I know:** My manual's rule is one table — the bomb's **light colour** decides the **wire colour to cut** (blue→yellow, green→white, red→red, white→green, yellow→blue). So the two facts I need are: the light's colour, and each wire's colour in position order 1–5. Blind has already told me his only action is `cut, position 1–5`, and he can't read colours or print by touch.

**Who reaches whom:** I cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so nothing from me reaches Blind directly. My only output is gestures, and only Deaf sees them. Deaf can speak, and both Blind and I can hear. So the chain is exactly: Deaf's eyes → my manual → Deaf's voice → Blind's hand. My job this turn is to request the two facts from Deaf in a way that decodes without any shared spoken code.

**How I'll encode:** Deaf never heard Blind's "starter code" (Deaf hears nothing), so I must teach it by gesture alone. A finger-count run ☝✌🤟🖖🖐 is close to self-explanatory as "one through five" — and it plants the code I'll need next round, when my whole answer to Deaf will be a single finger-count: the cut position. My first two calls echo the 🫴 "report/give" that Deaf already saw in Blind's wave: attention — report. Then "the top part — give it" (the light), then "the lower five, in order" (the wires). I close with 👍 from Blind's proposed yes-code as a general confirm. Deaf can answer in plain colour words — no cipher needed on the reporting leg, so there is nothing to mis-key on the most dangerous hop.

**Next round:** once Deaf names the light colour, I look it up, find which position holds the cut-colour, and send Deaf that one number.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🫴"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

**Encoding it:** Deaf has confirmed the full code — five is the open hand, and the agreed pattern is a number sign followed by thumbs-up meaning "cut that wire." I send 🖐 👍. I deliberately send nothing else: Deaf said any extra signs would be read as new code proposals, and this is the one leg where the meaning must be unambiguous, since it becomes Blind's spoken order. **After this:** once Deaf voices "cut wire five," the defusal should be done. If Deaf reports back that the board state changed (a new light colour, for instance), I'll look the rule up again next round. Until then, no questions, no extras.

It travels as a separate call, so it cannot delay or blur the instruction ahead of it.

**Standing ready:** if the board state changes after the cut — new light colour, new display — I re-run the table next round. Deaf's palm-down = press is noted, though my manual so far gives no press rule.
